messages:
john: Heads-up — we saw a spike of requests with tokens that include BOTH org_id and project_id claims. Some of these are routed as org-level and billed to the org, others routed to the project. Need a canonical resolution order and how the Console should surface the effective identity.

anya: Do we have a repro example? logs or token dump (redacted) would help.

john: pasted redacted jwt header/payload in thread: `eyJhbGciOi...`, payload: {\"sub\":\"sa-123\", \"org_id\":\"org-A\", \"project_id\":\"proj-9\", \"iss\":\"auth.internal\"} — proxy is setting origin-header sometimes, and legacy minting produced both claims.

renee: My 2c: routing should prefer the most specific claim (project over org) for quota attribution. Otherwise customers with project-level budgets get surprised.

leo: +1 on specificity, but what about admin intents? If a service account is owned by org-A but granted project access, we must ensure logs show both canonical subject and granting entity. Console needs to show "effective subject" + "presented claims" so ops can debug.

anya: Telemetry wise we should add `effective_identity` tag to request traces and to quota events. That will let billing/alerts correlate mismatched attributions. Also add a boolean `had_both_scope_claims` for spike detection.

john: Implementation options: 1) Resolve routing by precedence: project_id > org_id; 2) Keep current behavior but add warning logs and surface mismatch in Console; 3) Introduce explicit `scope_resolution` claim at mint-time that unambiguously sets routing. Thoughts?

renee: Option 3 is ideal for long term (explicit), but rollout is harder. Option 1 is safe and fast. If we do 1, we must run a preflight job to surface how many tokens would flip attribution.

leo: Agreed. Preflight: run a sampling pass on last 7 days of traces, count requests where project_id != null and org_id != null, show current attribution vs proposed (project-preferred). Add sample list of top customers impacted.

anya: UX: Console should show a tooltip on the request detail: "Routing decision: project-preferred (project_id present) — Attribution changed from org-A to proj-9" and link to docs. Also expose a deprecation banner for tokens that still include both claims.

john: Rollout plan proposal: feature flag `scope_resolution_project_preferred` default OFF. 1) Run preflight query. 2) Enable flag in canary region for 1% traffic + telemetry logging. 3) Evaluate mismatch rate, unauthorized/errors, billing deltas for 72h. 4) If OK, ramp to 100% and create migration docs for customers.

renee: Metrics to watch: attribution-flip-rate, request-error-rate, quota-exceeded-events, billing-change-estimate, support-tickets (track tags). Make a dashboard with those 5.

leo: Also add an alert: if attribution-flip-rate > 0.5% for any single customer over 24h, auto rollback flag for that customer and page eng-oncall.

anya: I'll add the telemetry fields and mock Grafana dashboard. John/Leo — can you produce the preflight query and the list of top impacted customers by EOD?

john: On it. I have a job draft: `SELECT count(*) as c, org_id, project_id, current_attribution FROM requests WHERE ts > now() - interval '7 days' GROUP BY org_id, project_id, current_attribution ORDER BY c desc LIMIT 50;` Will run in staging first.

ops-bot: deploy scheduled: telemetry-schema-v2 -> staging at 2025-03-18T22:30:00Z

renee: Good. One more UX point: when Console shows request timeline, include a small badge: `Attribution: project` or `Attribution: org` and on hover show the raw claims. That saves a support back-and-forth.

john: Ok team — we'll do preflight + dashboard + feature flagged canary. Meeting to reconvene after preflight results. Thanks. :thumbsup:
